newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S&P ups Handelsbanken outlook to positive.
newsitem.headline: S&P ups Handelsbanken outlook to positive.

text.p: U.S. credit ratings agency Standard & Poor's on Tuesday affirmed Swedish bank Handelsbanken ratings and raised its outlook to positive from stable.
S&P said the revision of the outlook for Handelsbanken reflects the continuing improvement in the bank's financial profile and its strong market position.
"SHB's (Handelsbanken's) financial profile is continuing to improve, drive by increased revenues, very good cost efficiency and lower credit losses," S&P said in a statement.
"Additionally, revenues are strengthening despite a tough competitive operating environment in the domestic market."
The agency said Handelsbanken has an important position in the Swedish banking sector as the largest bank by asset size.

"Additionally the bank is positioning itself to be a major player in the other Nordic countries where its cost efficiencies will be a strong competitive advantage in competing for new business," it said.
S&P affirmed the bank's rating of A+ for senior unsecured debt, A+ for counterparty rating long-term, A for subordinated debt, A-1 for commercial paper and A-1 for counterparty rating short-term.
